context.title: The Son of God Crucified
context.summary: Pilate releases Barabbas and hands Jesus over. Soldiers mock him, Simon of Cyrene carries his cross, and Jesus is crucified at Golgotha. He cries out and dies, the temple veil tears, and Joseph of Arimathea buries him.
context.background: Pontius Pilate governed Judea for Rome from about AD 26 to 36. Mark marks time carefully: crucified at the third hour (9 a.m.), darkness from the sixth to the ninth hour (noon to 3 p.m.). Simon is named as father of Alexander and Rufus, apparently people Mark's readers knew.

customs.note: Aramaic for 'place of a skull,' a site just outside Jerusalem's walls. Executions were held beside roads to warn passers-by.
The day before the Sabbath, when work was finished ahead of rest. Bodies had to be dealt with before sundown.

watchFor: Jesus' cry 'Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?' quotes Psalm 22:1 (v. 34).
A Roman centurion says, 'Truly this man was the Son of God' (v. 39), echoing 1:1.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Pontius
people.summary: Probably connected with the Roman family of the Pontii, and called “Pilate” from the Latin pileatus, i.e., “wearing the pileus”, which was the “cap or badge of a manumitted slave,” as indicating that he was a “freedman,” or the descendant of one.

people.name: Barabbas
people.summary: I.e., son of Abba or of a father, a notorious robber whom Pilate proposed to condemn to death instead of Jesus, whom he wished to release, in accordance with the Roman custom (John 18:40; Mark 15:7; Luke 23:19).

people.name: Simon
people.summary: A Jew of Cyrene, in North Africa, then a province of Libya. A hundred thousand Jews from Palestine had been settled in this province by Ptolemy Soter (B.C. 323-285), where by this time they had greatly increased in number.

people.name: Alexander
people.summary: A man whose father, Simon the Cyrenian, bore the cross of Christ (Mark 15:21).

people.name: Elijah
people.summary: “The Tishbite,” the “Elias” of the New Testament, is suddenly introduced to our notice in 1 Kings 17:1 as delivering a message from the Lord to Ahab.

people.name: James
people.summary: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature.

people.name: Mary
people.summary: A surname derived from Magdala, the place of her nativity, given to one of the Marys of the Gospels to distinguish her from the other Marys (Matt. 27:56, 61; 28:1, etc.).

people.name: Salome
people.summary: The wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John (Mat. 27:56), and probably the sister of Mary, the mother of our Lord (John 19:25). She sought for her sons places of honour in Christ’s kingdom (Matt. 20:20, 21; comp. 19:28).

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: A native of Arimathea, probably the Ramah of the Old Testament (1 Sam. 1:19), a man of wealth, and a member of the Sanhedrim (Matt. 27:57; Luke 23:50), an “honourable counsellor, who waited for the kingdom of God.”

places.name: Cyrene
places.summary: A city (now Tripoli) in Upper Libya, North Africa, founded by a colony of Greeks (B.C. 630). It contained latterly a large number of Jews, who were introduced into the city by Ptolemy, the son of Lagus, because he thought they would contribute to the security of the place.

places.name: Golgotha
places.summary: The common name of the spot where Jesus was crucified. It is interpreted by the evangelists as meaning “the place of a skull” (Matt. 27:33; Mark 15:22; John 19:17).

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Arimathea
places.summary: A “city of the Jews” (Luke 23:51), the birth-place of Joseph in whose sepulchre our Lord was laid (Matt. 27:57, 60; John 19:38). It is probably the same place as Ramathaim in Ephraim, and the birth-place of Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1, 19).

events.title: Holy Week
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 21:1 – John 20:31. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 8 days.

events.title: Roman Trials
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 27:11 – John 19:16. People: Jesus, Simon, Pontius, Barabbas. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: Bearing Cross to Golgotha
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 27:32 – John 19:17. People: Jesus, Simon. Place: Golgotha.

events.title: Crucifixion and Burial
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 27:35 – John 19:42. People: Jesus, Mary, Mother of Zebedees children, Joseph, Pontius, Salome. Place: Golgotha.
